messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary deploy finished for service-infer at 2026-03-15T04:23Z. image=redwood/infer:20260315-rc -> digest=sha256:fa7b9c...

devon: seeing increased 5xxs and latency on canary nodes immediately after that deploy. spikes from ~20ms -> 800ms. rolling back?

maya: I can confirm 5xx surge on canary, failing on forward model loads. Crash loops on two pods. `kubectl get pods -l app=service-infer,env=canary` shows CrashLoopBackOff on infer-worker-*.

kai: hmm, deploy job logs show the promoted tag points to two different digests depending on the build agent. possible parallel build cache desync in CI.

anne: @devon visible in deploy job: promotion step used `promo-latest` which resolved to digest sha256:fa7b9c on agent A and sha256:b3d2ef on agent B. both got pushed under the same tag due to registry race.

devon: that matches the symptom: half the canary pods pulled one digest, half the other. the failing digest seems to be the one built on agent B.

maya: customer impact? any production traffic hit? we route 10% to canary. some users might see inference errors/timeouts. need to kill new routing immediately.

deploy-bot: paging oncall: @maya assigned (P1) — new canary showing 40% error rate for requests proxied to canary. Incident created: INC-20260315-007.

maya: I'm toggling the routing feature flag to force 0% canary. running: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/toggle -d '{"service":"infer","target":"canary","pct":0}'`

kai: also pausing auto-scaler to avoid churn: `kubectl scale --replicas=1 deployment/infer-canary`

anne: confirm feature flag flip acknowledged by console, traffic routed back to stable. latency and 5xxs dropping back to baseline.

devon: good. next steps: identify bad digest and prevent promotion. where did tag race occur? CI job graph shows two parallel builders (bldr-3 and bldr-7) both pushed with `docker push $TAG` without using immutable digests.

sre-lead: that's the root cause: mutable tag promotion during parallel builds. mitigation: revert to push-as-digest and promote by digest, or serialize tag mutation.

maya: for immediate mitigation we should: 1) mark the bad digest unauthenticated/disabled in registry, 2) revoke the tag alias, 3) backfill CI to stop parallel tag writes.

kai: I can add a temporary registry policy to deny tag writes to `redwood/infer:20260315-rc` and set promotion job to fail safe. Running registry ACL update now.

deploy-bot: registry: tag-protect rule applied to redwood/infer:20260315-rc by kai. New pushes to that tag will be rejected.

anne: I've opened a ticket in CI (CI-1428) to change the promotion step to publish digests and update deployment manifests to reference digests, not mutable tags.

devon: we still need to perform a full sweep: list all images with this tag across regions, verify which digest is running where. command: `gcrctl list-tags redwood/infer --filter "tag=20260315-rc"`

maya: runbook note: if we need emergency rollback for customer-facing canaries, use the kill-switch `flags/route-infer` and escalate to SRE lead for cross-region rollbacks.

kai: audit done: two digest variants found. Marked bad digest sha256:b3d2ef as non-deployable. Removing from canary registries in ap-south and eu-west.

devon: we've redeployed canary pods to the stable digest (sha256:fa7b9c) where appropriate. healthchecks green. errors gone.

maya: handoff time — I'm oncall for another 20m then handing to @kai. Summary: P1 canary error caused by parallel CI tag race -> partial promotion of bad digest -> 10% traffic experienced errors -> feature flag kill-switch used -> registry rule applied -> promotion job fix ticket opened -> verified cleanup across regions.

kai: taking over. I'll monitor for 1h, follow up on CI-1428, and schedule a postmortem.

devon: please add timeline and notes to INC-20260315-007 and tag relevant customer accounts that might have seen errors. Reach out to solutions-eng for user comms if needed.

pagerduty: Note: On-call handoff from maya to kai recorded at 2026-03-15T05:10Z.

maya: quick PSA: avoid `promo-latest` style tags in pipelines; prefer immutability. Will add to infra changelog. :memo:

sre-lead: Thanks team. We'll run a short postmortem tomorrow, include CI, registry, and deployment runbooks. Good catch & fast mitigation. :thumbsup:
